protocol: D-000 new cycle after CONTESTED D-099, turn 1 of 3; not a fourth turn of D-099; refute not confirm; PREFERENCE-LADEN scoped D-006 fleet-class successor plus RULE-GOVERNED naming of the v3 reserved G03/G04 identifiers
summary: Almost all of this cycle lands, and the two findings I raised at D-099 turn 3 are both correctly diagnosed: PROC_PIDARCHINFO really is absent from MacOSX15.4.sdk (I confirmed the absence directly), and PROC_PIDTBSDINFO really does carry pbi_start_tvsec/pbi_start_tvusec while proc_bsdshortinfo carries no start time at all. The start-identity repair is right, is size-checked, and is now compared against S1 as D099-T3-SF-1 asked. The AT_PLATFORM dereference is right. The 18-of-18 arithmetic is right, and I checked it against D-002's enumerated required-gate set rather than trusting the register's own subtotal. But the centerpiece — the replacement process-arch observation — does not observe the process. I compiled the recipe and ran it. On this arm64 host, sysctl.proc_cputype returns CPU_TYPE_ARM64 for a native arm64 process, for launchd, and for a live Mach-O x86_64 process running under Rosetta, whose translation I confirmed in the same breath through the draft's own step 6 (P_TRANSLATED=1). The field returns the host's CPU type, not the target's. It cannot tell a translated x86_64 process from a native arm64 one, which is the exact discrimination the draft names it to perform. I have to record that this is partly my own doing: my D099-T3-MF-1 repair offered sysctl.proc_cputype as the sysctl-family alternative, and I offered it from reasoning rather than from measurement. This turn I measured it, and it does not hold.

objections.location: Subject, 'macOS target-process protocol (item 10)', step 5, and the acceptance conjunction in step 6
objections.claim: Step 5 designates the cpu_type_t returned by `sysctl.proc_cputype` with T appended as 'the process-arch field'. It is not. The MIB returns the HOST CPU type, adjusted only for the process's 64-bitness. It returns the identical value for a native arm64 process and for a live x86_64 process under Rosetta, so it performs no per-process discrimination and merely restates preflight item 3's H = `uname -m`. Step 6's acceptance conjunction 'H, E, and `sysctl.proc_cputype` all match the class' is therefore a two-term test presented as a three-term test.
objections.why: I did not argue this from headers or from memory; I built it and ran it, because my own turn-3 suggestion is what put this call in the draft and I owed it a measurement. First I confirmed the draft's premises, all of which are true: `PROC_PIDARCHINFO` and `struct proc_archinfo` are absent from MacOSX15.4.sdk (grep over the SDK's include tree returns nothing), `PROC_PIDTBSDINFO` is 3 with `PROC_PIDTBSDINFO_SIZE` = sizeof(struct proc_bsdinfo) and `pbi_start_tvsec`/`pbi_start_tvusec` at proc_info.h:80-81, `struct proc_bsdshortinfo` has thirteen members and no timeval, `P_TRANSLATED` is 0x00020000 at proc.h:178, `CPU_TYPE_ARM64` is 0x0100000c and `CPU_TYPE_X86_64` is 0x01000007 at machine.h:104,111, and both `posix_spawnattr_setarchpref_np` and `POSIX_SPAWN_START_SUSPENDED` (0x0080) exist. So the draft's reasons for abandoning PROC_PIDARCHINFO and PROC_PIDT_SHORTBSDINFO are correct, and my turn-3 primary repair was itself wrong for this SDK. Then I implemented step 5 exactly as written — `sysctlnametomib("sysctl.proc_cputype", mib, &miblen)`, append T, `sysctl(mib, miblen+1, &cputype, &len, NULL, 0)` — and it works mechanically: the name resolves to MIB 0.102, miblen is 2, the call succeeds, and `len` is 4 = sizeof(cpu_type_t), so every reject branch in step 5 passes. That is the problem: it passes for the wrong reason. I queried three targets from an arm64 parent. Self (arm64): 0x0100000c. PID 1, launchd (arm64): 0x0100000c. A live `/tmp/spin_x86`, which `file` reports as 'Mach-O 64-bit executable x86_64' and which was RUNNING at query time (kill -0 succeeded, ps STAT 'RN'): 0x0100000c. The x86_64 target returned ARM64. To rule out any doubt that the target was genuinely translated, I read the draft's own step 6 on the same two live PIDs in the same run: the x86_64 process reported p_flag=0x00034004, P_TRANSLATED=1; a native arm64 process reported p_flag=0x00004004, P_TRANSLATED=0. So step 6 discriminates perfectly and step 5 does not discriminate at all. The behaviour is consistent with the kernel deriving the value from `cpu_type()` and clearing CPU_ARCH_ABI64 for non-64-bit processes, which is also why `sysctl.proc_translated` has to exist as a separate MIB. On macos-15 the value is ARM64 for every process on the box; on macos-15-intel it will be X86_64 for every process on the box. Step 5's accepted-value table is satisfied by the host alone. I want to be exact about the blast radius, because it is narrower than the finding's severity might suggest and the coordinator should not over-repair. The protocol as a whole is still fail-closed against the thing it fears: step 1 pins exactly one CPU type through `posix_spawnattr_setarchpref_np` with close-match fallback forbidden, so an x86_64-only image cannot spawn on macos-15 at all; step 6 rejects on P_TRANSLATED=1; step 2 rejects fat images; D binds the on-disk bytes. No translated measurement gets counted. What fails is not the safety of the contract but its stated warrant — and the warrant is the entire reason this cycle exists. D-098 was CONTESTED precisely on 'the process-architecture recipe still observes the inspector ... not the launched target process', D-099 was CONTESTED on the same field naming a struct member that does not exist, and the dispatch for this cycle lists 'process arch still observes the inspector or a fat slice' as a named attack. A host-scoped MIB observes the inspector's machine. The defect class survives its third cycle in a new disguise: D-098 read the inspector's own image, D-099 read a nonexistent member, D-101 reads a real member of the wrong subject. Writing 'named' into file 08 on the strength of a contract that asserts a per-process observation it does not make is the specific thing condition 4 is supposed to prevent, since condition 4's other half is 'no document claims QUALIFIED or DEMONSTRATED without retained evidence' and this is a claim about what the retained evidence will show.
objections.repair: Stop looking for a per-process CPU-type API on this SDK; on MacOSX15.4.sdk there is not one on any route discussed across D-099 or D-101, and step 5 should say so rather than name a fourth candidate. The draft already holds everything needed to derive the field soundly. Replace step 5 with the derivation the contract can actually defend: the target's ISA is determined by H (preflight item 3, `uname -m`) together with `P_TRANSLATED` read from T's own kinfo_proc in step 6 — on macos-15, P_TRANSLATED=0 means the target is arm64 and P_TRANSLATED=1 means it is x86_64 and rejects; on macos-15-intel, H is x86_64 and no translation exists to consider — corroborated by E (the on-disk thin slice, item 3), by D (the digest binding, step 3), and by the single-CPU-type spawn preference in step 1 which makes any other ISA unspawnable rather than merely detectable. That is four independent bindings and it is stronger than the one the draft claims, so this costs the contract nothing. Then fix step 6's conjunction to name what it actually tests: H, E and P_TRANSLATED. If the coordinator wants a genuine per-process ISA read on Darwin for its own sake, the honest options are `task_for_pid` plus reading the running image's Mach-O header from the target's memory, both of which need entitlements the hosted runner will not grant — which is itself worth one sentence in Alternatives, so that a fourth cycle does not go looking for this API again. Please also record, in whatever form the entry uses for this, that D099-T3-MF-1's suggested sysctl-family alternative was measured this turn and rejected; I raised it and it is my error to flag, and leaving it unmarked invites its return.

notesNonBlocking.location: Subject, 'Governed series (G04)' against the two per-release launch protocols
notesNonBlocking.observation: The launch protocols are headed 'G03/G04 help/version' and enumerate one cold and one warm launch per command per VM, so the G04 help/version RSS samples and the G03 latency samples come from the same launches. The contract never says how either RSS quantity is obtained. 'peak RSS' can be taken from wait4/getrusage after exit with zero perturbation, but 'steady baseline RSS' for a --help that lives on the order of the 100 ms cold p50 bound requires sampling the process while it runs, and doing that on a shared launch perturbs the co-measured G03 latency. I record rather than raise it because DR-G04's own evidence column in file 08 is 'raw RSS traces and methodology', which routes methodology to the gate's qualification evidence, and because this entry says 'not authored' in both inserted cells. The tension is real but it belongs to the harness author, not to the naming act.
